statement: Show that the tangent to the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=r^{2}$ at a point $(x_{0},y_{0})$ on it has equation $x_{0}x+y_{0}y=r^{2}$, and prove this tangent is perpendicular to the radius to $(x_{0},y_{0})$.
solution: Implicitly, $2x+2yy'=0$ so $y'=-x/y$; at $(x_{0},y_{0})$ the tangent gradient is $-x_{0}/y_{0}$. The tangent through $(x_{0},y_{0})$ is $y-y_{0}=-\tfrac{x_{0}}{y_{0}}(x-x_{0})$, i.e. $x_{0}x+y_{0}y=x_{0}^{2}+y_{0}^{2}=r^{2}$. The radius has gradient $y_{0}/x_{0}$; the product of gradients is $(-x_{0}/y_{0})(y_{0}/x_{0})=-1$, so they are perpendicular. (Check at $(3,4)$ on $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$: tangent $3x+4y=25$, radius gradient $4/3$, tangent gradient $-3/4$.)
hints: Use implicit differentiation to get the tangent gradient.
Write the tangent line and rearrange to $x_{0}x+y_{0}y=r^{2}$.
Show the product of the two gradients is $-1$.
